description: AFG - Active Faults Greece: a comprehensive geomorphology-based 1:25,000 fault database is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by John G. Begg et al. Greece is Europe’s most seismically active country, as it is being deformed by an active subduction-system and one of the world’s fastest-spreading continental rifts. Onshore active faults pose seismic-hazard that cannot be reliably assessed in the absence of a complete map of potential earthquake sources. Coverage: global (GR); published in 2025. Formats: Excel, Shapefile. The data are held in GFZ Data Services and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
